title: Pavlovo
summary: Pavlovo refers to multiple inhabited localities primarily located in Russia, with a significant number of these localities being rural villages. While the name is prevalent in various Russian regions, it does not have a direct connection to [[ukraine|Ukraine]], yet its mention is relevant in the context of regional geography and historical ties between Ukraine and Russia.

sections.heading: General Overview
paragraphs: Pavlovo (Russian: Павлово) is a name shared by several inhabited localities across Russia, primarily consisting of rural villages.

sections.heading: Localities by Oblast
paragraphs: As of 2010, the following regions in Russia contain localities named Pavlovo:
In Arkhangelsk Oblast, there is Pavlovo, a village under the jurisdiction of Novodvinsk.
In Ivanovo Oblast, Pavlovo is a village located in Yuryevetsky District.
Kaliningrad Oblast features Pavlovo as a settlement in Novostroyevsky Rural Okrug of Ozyorsky District.
Kaluga Oblast has three villages named Pavlovo, situated in Borovsky, Kozelsky, and Mosalsky Districts respectively.
Kirov Oblast includes two villages named Pavlovo, found in Pizhansky and Sanchursky Districts.
Kostroma Oblast has four villages named Pavlovo, located in Galichsky, Kologrivsky, Parfenyevsky, and Sharyinsky Districts.
Leningrad Oblast contains three localities named Pavlovo, including an urban-type settlement in Kirovsky District and two villages in Kingiseppsky and Vsevolozhsky Districts.
In Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, there are four localities named Pavlovo, including a town in Pavlovsky District and three villages in various districts.
Novgorod Oblast features three rural localities named Pavlovo, found in Krestetsky, Lyubytinsky, and Maryovsky Districts.
Novosibirsk Oblast has one locality named Pavlovo, a selo in Vengerovsky District.
Oryol Oblast includes two villages named Pavlovo, located in Trosnyansky and Zalegoshchensky Districts.
Perm Krai has one village named Pavlovo in Ordinsky District.
Pskov Oblast has eleven localities named Pavlovo, distributed across various districts.
Ryazan Oblast contains one village named Pavlovo in Klepikovsky District.
Smolensk Oblast has six villages named Pavlovo, located in different districts.
Tomsk Oblast features one locality named Pavlovo, a selo in Kargasoksky District.
Tula Oblast includes two villages named Pavlovo in Aleksinsky and Shchyokinsky Districts.
Tver Oblast has six villages named Pavlovo across various districts.
Udmurt Republic contains one village named Pavlovo in Uvinsky District.
Vladimir Oblast has one village named Pavlovo in Petushinsky District.
Vologda Oblast features eleven villages named Pavlovo in several districts.
Yaroslavl Oblast includes eight localities named Pavlovo, found in different rural okrugs.
